summary: Iteration 16 — Daily founder digest backend testing. 9/10 pytest checks pass. Endpoints exist and most behaviour matches spec: auth gating, jury 403, /preview HTML branding + counts + is_test exclusion, anonymous voice tryouts excluded from the list but counted, force=true sends + persists system_state, scheduler startup log present, explicit force=false dedupes correctly. ONE SPEC-VIOLATING BUG: POST /api/founder/digest/send default `force` value is True in server.py — review spec says force=false must be the default and dedupe by default. Today calling /send without any query param bypasses dedupe and re-sends the email every time.

critical.issue: Default value of `force` query parameter is True (server.py:330 `force: bool = True`). Review spec requires force=false as the default so back-to-back calls dedupe. Today the default call ALWAYS sends, persists system_state with today's date, and returns {sent: true}. Without `?force=false` explicitly set, dedupe never engages. Explicit `?force=false` works correctly (returns {sent: false, reason: 'already_sent_today'}); explicit `?force=true` correctly bypasses dedupe.

action_items: Change server.py line 330 from `force: bool = True` to `force: bool = False` so the manual trigger endpoint defaults to deduped behaviour (matching review spec). QA can still bypass with `?force=true`.
critical_code_review_comments: daily_digest.send_digest_now persists system_state on EVERY send (including force=true). That means a single force=true call will block the regular 07:00 UTC scheduler send for that day, since the scheduler runs with force=False. Acceptable for QA but worth a comment in the docstring.

daily_digest._collect uses ISO-string comparison on `created_at` ($gte cutoff.isoformat()). That works because all writes also serialize to ISO. If any future code writes datetime objects directly into Mongo this filter will silently drop those rows.

scheduler_loop catches everything and sleeps until next hour — good. But there is no guard against running twice if start_scheduler is called twice during dev hot-reload; consider an idempotency flag on app.state.

render_html injects user-supplied fields (presale.name/company/plan_interest, voice transcript, email) directly into HTML with no escaping. A signup with `<script>` in the name would render as raw HTML in the digest email inbox. Not exploitable end-to-end (email clients sandbox JS), but worth html.escape() on user fields.

rca of the issue: Root cause: server.py:330 — `async def founder_send_digest(user=Depends(get_founder_user), force: bool = True)`. The default value of `force` was set to True, presumably to make manual QA triggers fire immediately. However, the review spec explicitly requires `force=false` to be the default so two back-to-back manual calls dedupe. Reproduction: (1) DELETE db.system_state document _id='daily_digest' (or wait until tomorrow); (2) POST /api/founder/digest/send with no query string → returns {sent: true} and writes today's date to system_state; (3) POST /api/founder/digest/send again with no query string → STILL returns {sent: true} (BUG — should be {sent: false, reason: 'already_sent_today'}). Mitigation: change default to False in server.py. Confirmed via direct probes: explicit ?force=false dedupes correctly, explicit ?force=true bypasses correctly — only the implicit default is wrong.
